chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Names of God and their derivation — from what is 'Allah' derived?

He said: So he said to me: 'O Hisham! Allah is derived from ilah (deity), and ilah requires a worshipper (ma'luh). And the name is other than the named. So whoever worships the name without the meaning (reality) has disbelieved and has not worshipped anything; and whoever worships the name and the meaning has disbelieved and worshipped two; and whoever worships the meaning without the name — that is tawhid. Do you understand, O Hisham?'

He said: So I said, 'Give me more.' He said: 'Indeed, God has ninety-nine names. If the name were the named, then every one of them would be a deity. But God is a meaning (reality) toward which these names point, and all of them are other than Him. O Hisham! Bread is a name for food, water is a name for the drink, cloth is a name for what is worn, fire is a name for what burns. Do you understand, O Hisham, an understanding with which you can repel and fight our enemies and those who take others alongside God — Majestic and Mighty?' I said: 'Yes.'
He said: So he said: 'May God benefit you with it and affirm you, O Hisham.' Hisham said: By God, no one overcame me regarding tawhid until I reached my present station.

key_terms.إله: Ilah — deity, that which is worshipped; the root from which Allah is derived
key_terms.الاسم: The name — a linguistic designation, a pointer
key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid — divine unity; worshipping the Reality alone
key_terms.المسمى: The named — the actual reality being designated
key_terms.المعنى: The meaning/reality — the actual Divine Being being pointed to
key_terms.مأكولاً: Worshipper, one who worships (the ilah requires a ma'luh)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Name of God and God Himself according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith records a celebrated theological exchange between Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) concerning the ontological distinction between God's Names and God's essential reality. The Imam articulates a precise philosophical point: the word 'Allah' is linguistically derived from 'ilah' (deity/worshipped one), and a deity by definition requires a worshipper. However, the name itself — as a linguistic label — is not identical to the Divine Reality it designates. Worshipping only the label without understanding the transcendent reality is kufr (disbelief); equally, treating the name as a second entity alongside the reality is polytheism (worshipping two). True tawhid consists in directing worship exclusively to the Divine Reality, using names merely as pointers. This teaching was conveyed to Hisham ibn al-Hakam, the foremost Imami theologian of his era, who used this insight as the cornerstone of his argumentation against opponents of Imami theology in the disputatious intellectual environment of early Abbasid Baghdad.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
‘He asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Names of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and their deriving Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from what He<sup>azwj</sup> is Derived’.

So heasws said to me: ‘O Hisham! Allahazwj is derived from ‘God’ and ‘The God’, it requires its worshipper. And the name is other than the named. So the one who worships the Name besides the Meaning, so he has blasphemed and has not worshipped anything; and the one who worships the Name and the Meaning, so he has blasphemed and has worshipped two; and the one who worships the Meaning besides the Name, so that is the Tawheed (Oneness). Do you understand, O Hisham?’

He (Hisham) said, ‘So I said, ‘Increase it for me’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> there are ninety nine Names, and if it was such that the Name was the Named, it would be so that every Name from these would be a God. But, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Meaning which these Names Indicate upon, and all of these are other than Him<sup>azwj</sup>. O Hisham! The bread is a name of the food, and the water is a name of the drink, and the cloth is a name of the garment, and the fire is a name of the incinerator. Do you understand, O Hisham? (It is) an understanding you can repulse and fight our<sup>asws</sup> enemies with it and the ones who taking others along with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty’. I said, ‘Yes’.

He (Hisham) said, ‘So heasws said: ‘May Allahazwj Benefit you with it and Affirm you, O Hisham!’. Hisham said, ‘So, by Allahazwj! No one was able to subdue me regarding the Tawheed (Oneness) until I rose to this status of mine’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who asked Imam abu ’Abdallah (a.s.) about the names of Allah and about the root or derivative forms of those names. “What is the root word for Allah?”

The Imam replied, “The word Allah is derived from the word Elah (Lord) which requires Ma’luh (some one whose Lord one has become). Note that names are something other than whatever to which they apply. O Hissham, whoever, worships the name without the fact for which the name stands he has denied the existence of Allah and has not worshipped any thing. Whoever worships the name and the meaning for which the name stands he has worshipped two things. Whoever worships the meaning without the name he is a monotheist. Did you understand it ) O Hisham?”

Hisham then asked, “Please explain further.” The Imam then said, “Allah has ninety nine names. If names would have been the samething for which they stand every one of them would have been a Lord. However, Allah is a meaning for which these names stand and they all are something other than Him. O Hisham, bread is the name for a certain kind of food, water is the name for a certain kind of drink, cloth is the name for a certain kind of garment and fire is the name for a thing that burns. Did you understand, O Hisham, in a form of understanding that would help you to defend our cause against our enemies and those who worship things that are other than Allah?” I said, “Yes, I did receive such understanding.”

The Imam then said, “May Allah grant you success in it and keep you steadfast (in your belief). Hisham has said, “I swear by Allah that since then no one has been able to defeat me in an argumentation on the issue of the Oneness of Allah and that has made me reach this position that I hold.”
